rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a heat treatment to form Cr-rich secondary phases in a single-phase fcc HEA, while the paper applied thermal aging to an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA to control L12 ordering and phase boundary morphology. These are different kinds of interventions (phase formation vs. ordering control).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies intermediate temperature deformation and a heat treatment for phase formation, whereas the paper uses specific aging temperatures (600°C and 750°C) without deformation to study a ductile-brittle-ductile transition. The regimes differ fundamentally.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes grain boundary nanosegregation reducing cohesion, while the paper's mechanism involves L12 ordering restricting cross-slip and jagged phase boundaries causing stress concentration. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved toughness with treatment, while the paper reports a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition with minimum ductility at 600°C. The predicted property direction and behavior are contradictory.
